analysis.one_liner: Max Healthcare Institute runs a network of premium hospitals concentrated in Delhi NCR and North India, under sole promoter Abhay Soi.
tags: PAT fall is a tax base-effect
analysis.whats_happening: Max Healthcare reported Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026 quarter) results on Oct 30, 2026: consolidated revenue rose 20% YoY to ₹2,569 crore and EBITDA rose 24% to ₹712 crore (margin up to 27.7% from 26.9%), but reported net profit fell 15.6% YoY to ₹414 crore. Separately, reports of a proposed 30% NPPA trade-margin cap on 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs pulled the stock down roughly 20% over three weeks in October 2026, since oncology is close to a fifth of Max's revenue.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a hospital chain, not a pharma or insurance company - it earns from bed occupancy, surgeries, diagnostics and pharmacy sales within its own hospitals. The scary-looking '15.6% profit drop' headline is mostly a tax accounting artifact, not a business slowdown - last year's quarter had a one-off tax credit tied to a merger that didn't repeat. On the metric management itself uses (network PAT, including hospitals run under management contracts), profit actually grew 10%. The real live risk is a government price cap on cancer drug margins, which could structurally dent a meaningful slice of revenue going forward - that's separate from, and more durable than, this one quarter's tax noise.
analysis.quarters: Revenue has risen steadily for five straight quarters: ₹2,135 cr (Q2 FY26) → ₹2,068 cr (Q3 FY26) → ₹2,143 cr (Q4 FY26) → ₹2,366 cr (Q1 FY27) → ₹2,569 cr (Q2 FY27). EBITDA has moved broadly in step, and EBITDA margin actually expanded this quarter. The one number that looks odd - PAT of ₹414 cr in Q2 FY27 versus ₹491 cr a year ago - is NOT comparable: the year-ago quarter carried a roughly ₹149 cr one-off tax benefit linked to the Crosslay Remedies/Jaypee Healthcare merger, which flipped tax expense from a ₹45 cr credit then to a ₹126 cr charge now. Strip that out and underlying (network-basis) PAT grew 10% YoY to ₹448 crore. Management flagged faster occupancy ramp-up on newly added beds and growing medical-value-travel (foreign patient) volumes as the drivers of the top-line growth.
analysis.performance_read: There have been no splits or demergers here (has_corporate_action: false), so the price series can be read at face value - this is a genuine, not an accounting-driven, move. The uncomfortable fact: the stock is down 33.7% from its July 2025 peak of ₹1,297.59 and is sitting near its 52-week low of ₹815, against a last close of ₹860. It has badly underperformed both the Nifty and its closest listed peer, Apollo Hospitals, over the last quarter (-21.7% vs Nifty -5.5% and peer -5.6%) and the last year (-26.9% vs Nifty -10.9% and peer +8.7%). Zoom out further, though, and the picture flips: over 5 years the stock has returned 152.5%, well ahead of both the Nifty (28.6%) and Apollo (97.5%) - so this is a strong long-term compounder that has given back a large chunk of recent gains, not a structural underperformer.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades at a rich P/E of roughly 60-70x (figures vary slightly by source and date) and P/B of around 7.6-10x, against an ROE of about 14-15% and ROCE of roughly 13-15%. Why it commands this premium: Max is one of the few large, listed, pure-play premium hospital networks in India's most profitable healthcare market (Delhi NCR), with a scarce-asset quality and visible bed-capacity growth (+20% YoY) plus medical-tourism optionality. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question - a P/E multiple this far above the ROE it is currently generating is pricing in a lot of future growth, and the recent 34% drawdown shows the market is already re-rating that growth assumption down in response to the oncology margin-cap overhang.
analysis.growth_read: This is growth that is both volume- and margin-led, the healthier combination: network gross revenue was up 20% YoY, driven by a 20% YoY increase in bed capacity (to 6,184 beds) with management citing faster-than-usual occupancy ramp-up on the new beds, while EBITDA margin simultaneously expanded (26.9% to 27.7%). Flat or margin-only growth would be a weaker signal; here the underlying volumes are expanding alongside profitability.
analysis.health_read: On a network basis, EBITDA is converting into profit reasonably well - PAT grew 10% in step with margin expansion. The headline consolidated PAT decline this quarter is a tax/accounting base effect, not a cash-conversion problem. Debt stood at about ₹3,795 crore as of September 2026, being used to fund an active capex programme (₹415 crore just approved for ~209 new brownfield beds across MSSH Noida, MSSH Vaishali and BLK Max). At roughly 1.3x annualised EBITDA, leverage looks moderate rather than alarming. The bigger concern here is business/regulatory risk - the NPPA's proposed cancer-drug margin cap - rather than financial risk from the balance sheet.
analysis.ownership_read: Abhay Soi is the sole promoter with a 23.71% stake as of September 2026, essentially flat versus 23.74% a year earlier, and promoter pledge stands at 0% - no leverage against the promoter's own holding. Institutional ownership is heavy (FIIs and DIIs together reported well over 50% of the register), though the individual category percentages sourced did not neatly reconcile to 100%, so treat the exact split with caution and verify on screener/BSE. No widely known individual retail investor could be confirmed on the register from available data.
strengths: EBITDA margin expanded from 26.9% to 27.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 even while the network added capacity.
Bed capacity grew 20% YoY to 6,184 beds, with management citing faster occupancy ramp-up on new beds - a sign of real demand absorption, not just supply addition.
Zero promoter pledge and a stable ~23.7% promoter stake show no financial stress at the promoter level.
5-year shareholder return of 152.5% has comfortably beaten both the Nifty (28.6%) and peer Apollo Hospitals (97.5%).
watchpoints: NPPA's proposed 30% trade-margin cap on 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs is estimated to hit Max's earnings by roughly 4% - oncology is close to a fifth of its revenue, a larger exposure than most peers.

Headline consolidated PAT fell 15.6% YoY in Q2 FY27 purely because a one-off tax credit in the year-ago quarter didn't repeat - a reminder to check tax-line notes before trusting any YoY PAT comparison from this company.
Stock is down 33.7% from its July 2025 peak and sitting near its 52-week low of ₹815, with sharp 3-month and 1-year underperformance versus both the Nifty and peer Apollo Hospitals.
Valuation remains rich (P/E ~60-70x, P/B ~7.6-10x) against a mid-teens ROE, leaving limited cushion if the oncology margin cap or further regulatory action compresses margins.
analysis.one_thing: Q3 FY27 results will show whether network-basis PAT growth (~10% ex one-offs this quarter) holds up once the NPPA cancer-drug margin cap is finalised and takes effect - that will test whether the ~4% EPS-impact estimate is accurate or understates the hit.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue (₹2,569 cr) and PAT (₹414-415 cr) figures were consistent across Business Standard, Zeebiz and Screener.in; the separate 'network PAT' figure (₹448 cr, +10% YoY) comes from company commentary and is not strictly comparable to the consolidated PAT line - flagged explicitly above. Valuation multiples (P/E 60-74x, P/B 7.6-10x, ROCE 12.7-15%) varied by source and date, so screener.in's figures were used as the primary reference. Shareholding percentages sourced via search (promoter 23.71%, FII 21.27%, DII 31.00%, public 3.28%) did not sum to 100% and should be independently verified on screener/BSE before relying on the exact split. Could not verify whether any marquee individual investor holds a stake.
